prohibited_recommendations: Do not exclude GBS on a normal early CSF protein: protein is often normal in the first week, and the areflexia and the NCS support the diagnosis [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not discharge her as functional: early GBS can progress to bulbar and respiratory failure within days, so she is observed as an inpatient.
Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
required_recommendations: Admit for serial respiratory and autonomic monitoring; IVIg is not routinely advised in mildly affected patients within 2 weeks of onset; treat if she loses the ability to walk unaided or develops bulbar, respiratory or autonomic involvement [EAN_PNS_2023].
Record the GBS disability score (grade 1 now: minor signs, able to run) and re-examine strength, gait and bulbar function at least daily during the progressive phase.

Repeat FVC, MIP and MEP at least twice daily while symptoms progress; escalate to ICU-level monitoring if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg or 60% predicted or by more than 30%, MIP becomes weaker than -40 cmH2O, or MEP falls below 40 cmH2O [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while symptoms progress.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, early AIDP (day 3, mildly affected and ambulant, with early electrodiagnostic abnormalities)

differential.key_features: Cannot be excluded at day 3; reconsider if progression continues beyond 8 weeks.
Raised in the ED, but the areflexia, the mild distal weakness and the demyelinating NCS are objective findings.
Areflexia and sensory symptoms are not features of myositis; CK normal; no myopathic units on EMG.
No tick on full skin and scalp inspection, and sensory symptoms are present.
No abdominal pain, psychiatric symptoms, hyponatraemia or autonomic features.
Episodic weakness with normal sensation and preserved reflexes; potassium normal here.

key_clinical_evidence: At day 3, CSF protein is often still normal; absent F-waves and H-reflexes are among the earliest NCS abnormalities, as here.

Bilateral distal weakness with reduced or absent reflexes, a normal CSF and a consistent NCS correspond to Brighton level 2, provisionally, because the nadir has not yet been reached (nadir within 4 weeks) [Brighton_2011]. The certainty level does not decide treatment.

Treatment follows disability and progression: at GBS disability grade 1, 3 days from onset, she is admitted and monitored, and IVIg or plasma exchange is started if she can no longer walk unaided or develops bulbar, respiratory or autonomic involvement [EAN_PNS_2023].
Tick paralysis is excluded by a full skin and scalp examination in rapid ascending weakness; none was found here.
The culture-confirmed Campylobacter enteritis is history; the diarrhoea counts in mEGOS, and serology is not needed [Walgaard_2011].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: CSF protein is normal in many patients in the first week of GBS; it does not exclude the diagnosis when the clinical picture and the NCS support it.
red_herrings.data_point: Normal CSF protein (34 mg/dL) at day 3
red_herrings.intended_effect: Imply that GBS is excluded and lead to early discharge.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Reduced and absent reflexes with mild distal weakness are objective signs, and the NCS shows a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy; anxiety does not make the deficit functional.
red_herrings.data_point: ED consideration of a functional neurological disorder in an anxious patient
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on a functional disorder and discharge her.

general.query: treatment of mildly affected patients early in Guillain-Barre syndrome

results.finding: IVIg or plasma exchange is not advised for very mildly affected patients who can walk unaided within the first 2 weeks of onset, for whom randomised evidence of benefit is lacking; treatment is considered if they deteriorate, lose the ability to walk unaided, or develop bulbar, autonomic or respiratory involvement.

Weakness in GBS reaches its nadir within 4 weeks, usually within 2 weeks; about 20% of patients develop respiratory failure needing mechanical ventilation, so early patients are admitted and monitored.

general.summary: Mildly affected patients who can walk unaided early in GBS are admitted and monitored rather than treated routinely; immunotherapy is considered on deterioration [EAN_PNS_2023, Leonhard_2019].

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL nerve conduction study. 1. Mildly to moderately prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in bilateral median and peroneal motor nerves; CMAP amplitudes preserved. 2. Absent sural sensory nerve action potentials bilaterally. 3. Absent F-waves bilaterally in median and peroneal nerves. 4. Absent H-reflex bilaterally. 5. EMG: no denervation activity. Pattern indicates a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with proximal involvement and preserved motor axon integrity.

quantitative_data.pattern: Demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with proximal involvement (absent F-waves and H-reflex)

case_body_concerns: Early-presentation case (day 3): CSF and EMG findings are deliberately minimal to test agent recognition that early studies may be normal in GBS. No fix required — this is by design.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions, 2 red herrings; early mild GBS with a normal CSF, where the scored behaviour is admission and monitoring, not immediate immunotherapy.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Three-day bilateral tingling, reduced reflexes and mild gait unsteadiness in a 22-year-old, 2 weeks after Campylobacter gastroenteritis.
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. B. is a 22-year-old college student presenting to the ED with a 3-day history of bilateral tingling in her hands and feet. She had a Campylobacter gastroenteritis 2 weeks ago, confirmed by stool culture at a student health center. She recovered fully. Three days ago she developed bilateral hand and foot tingling. Yesterday she noticed her reflexes seemed absent when she tested them with her roommate (nursing student). She reports very mild gait unsteadiness but denies frank weakness: she walked to the ED and can still run, though she feels unsteady doing so. She has no facial symptoms, no diplopia, no dysphagia, no breathlessness. She is very anxious. The ED physician considered a functional neurological disorder given the absence of obvious weakness.

neurological_exam.additional: Respiratory: breathing comfortably, speaks in full sentences. Cough effective.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. No facial weakness, no ptosis, no ophthalmoplegia. Bulbar function normal.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly unsteady — wide-based gait but able to walk. Slight difficulty with tandem gait.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild distal weakness: ankle dorsiflexion 4+/5 and finger abduction 4+/5 bilaterally. Otherwise 5/5 throughout the upper and lower extremities.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent bilateral Achilles, biceps and triceps reflexes. Trace bilateral patellar and brachioradialis reflexes. Plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral hand tingling and mild bilateral distal foot tingling. Vibration slightly reduced at bilateral great toes.

physical_exam.skin: Full skin and scalp inspection: no tick, no rash.
